title: I Let 3 AI Agents Take Over My Life. Only 1 Didn't Fail
key_facts: A PCMag reviewer gave the same everyday tasks to three AI agents: ChatGPT's Dots, Gemini's Spark and Meta's Muse.
Dots is available only on ChatGPT Pro (from $100 a month), Business and Enterprise plans; Spark comes with Gemini AI Pro ($20) or AI Ultra (from $100); Muse is free with optional paid plans from $20.
Instacart shopping: Dots added the ingredients to the cart without trouble; Muse got there slowly and added saffron that was not in the recipe; Spark could not access the account and froze.
Job hunting: only Dots linked to specific job listings; Muse and Spark linked to aggregate sites or expired positions.
Dinner reservation: Dots found a place with a 6:15 p.m. opening; Muse and Spark suggested places, some of which do not take reservations.
Inbox cleanup: Dots went through more than 15 years of marketing email and built a spreadsheet of over 700 senders; Spark could only give unsubscribe links.
All three handled a Warframe wiki-to-spreadsheet research task.
The reviewer concludes Dots worked best but is not worth $100 a month unless you have many simple online tasks, and that agents are not yet essential.
quote_evidence: ChatGPT’s Dots consistently worked the best in my testing, which isn't very surprising given the incredibly powerful GPT-6 Astra model behind it.
I don’t think signing up just for this feature makes sense unless you truly have a ton of relatively simple online tasks ripe for automation with AI agents.
Although I’m more impressed by AI agents now than I was a year ago, I still don’t think they’re anywhere near essential.
why_it_matters_hint: A hands-on comparison suggests the paid agent works best but none of the three is essential yet.
notes: Single reviewer, five tasks, not a lab benchmark. Author not named in the text read. PCMag's rating legend and author bio skipped.
